html:
On Easter Sunday 1722 the Dutch explorer Jacob Roggeveen reached Rapa Nui, the first European known to land there. He named it Easter Island.

Roggeveen was searching for a southern continent for the Dutch West India Company. His crew saw the great moai still standing and shot several islanders in a scuffle on the beach.

Spanish, British and French ships followed later in the century, including James Cook in 1774, who saw many moai already toppled. The visits brought trade goods and disease, but the worst harm came with the slave raids of the 1860s.
